video_title: Landry Shamet and John Turturro on the New York Knicks’ Championship Run

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on the surge in New York Knicks fans
quotes.excerpt: There's a lot of people all of a sudden who are Knicks fans.
quotes.quote: There's a lot of people all of a sudden who are Knicks fans. For years I've had season tickets. After Patrick Ewing left, I couldn't give my seats away.

quotes.speaker: Landry Shamet
quotes.summary_phrase: Landry Shamet on the atmosphere at Madison Square Garden
quotes.excerpt: The sound went straight up to the top of the arena and straight down.
quotes.quote: I was right behind OG Anunoby when I jumped in there a little bit. But the sound, it went straight up to the top of the arena and straight down. It wasn't even a sound. It felt like this. I've rarely seen the Garden like that.

quotes.speaker: Landry Shamet
quotes.summary_phrase: Landry Shamet on the team's resilience during the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: I thought there was a chance I could be out of the league.
quotes.quote: I thought there was a chance I could be out of the league. Turning camp deal to start the year again with the team I'm coming back to. It was me and Malcolm Brogdon really. They went Malcolm and Malcolm didn't retire and I'm like, what am I doing? What am I doing?

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on the Knicks' comeback against the Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: After Jalen Brunson hit a basket and then you drew a charge, I remember you drew that charge.
quotes.quote: There was a bunch of games. That Cleveland game, the 22-point game, after Jalen Brunson hit a basket and then you drew a charge, I remember you drew that charge. Then you hit a three-pointer. I have season tickets behind the Knicks bench, but I share them. Sometimes I ask for a closer seat, sometimes they're not available. So my son and I said, you know what, let's just get tickets in the 200s. So I was sitting up a little high and I was sitting with some pretty rowdy fans. And this guy was kind of wide, was drinking a lot, and we were down by 22 before your charge. He turns to me and goes, we got them just where we want them. I was like, you can be right of me.

quotes.speaker: Landry Shamet
quotes.summary_phrase: Landry Shamet on the anxiety of playing home playoff games
quotes.excerpt: The first time playing in a finals game at home, knowing what it meant to New Yorkers.
quotes.quote: Game 3 specifically, just the first time playing in a finals game at home, knowing what it meant to New Yorkers as a whole, let's just start there. Everything that was stacking, you're like, okay, this is a big night. And then now we're going through TSA screening, we're staying in a hotel, so now our home routine is completely thrown off, you're riding a bus over. I remember my level of anxiety that day, and I think I felt it on the whole city. I felt it walking out on the street that morning to get the day started. I felt everyone, and it felt like Game 3 to me was such an anomaly in that sense where I agree, it didn't feel like a home game, but there was so much, everybody was just so uptight everywhere.

quotes.speaker: Landry Shamet
quotes.summary_phrase: Landry Shamet on the team's resilience during the Atlanta series
quotes.excerpt: We had to have some pretty honest, tough conversations with each other.
quotes.quote: It got a little weird, we can all acknowledge that. They pushed us, and we had to have some pretty honest, tough conversations with each other. I'm a firm believer that you have to go through some sort of life-questioning circumstance like that was. That was not great basketball we were playing, and we were in a tough spot. Things felt weird. There's always a point where, okay, the coach is going to be really honest with you, he's going to call it how it is, we shoot you straight, practices are going to be uncomfortable, and there's a point and a fork in the road where you can decide to say, all right, maybe this isn't it, maybe this isn't our year, things aren't going right, things feel weird, or double down and go the other route, which is the route we went and rattled off 13 in a row.

quotes.speaker: Landry Shamet
quotes.summary_phrase: Landry Shamet on the team's offensive adjustment and playmaking
quotes.excerpt: We started really playing through Cade a lot too, like being our facilitator.
quotes.quote: We started really playing through Cade a lot too, like being our facilitator. Throwing him the ball and his assist numbers went through the roof. He was incredible, and we hadn't really asked him to do that all year. So to then just say, okay, this is what we got to do, and to his credit too, a guy like him who is a generational talent, for us to say, hey, we don't need you to score as much, we need you to get everybody else involved, and for him not even to like bat an eye. I think that to me was one of the moments being up close and personal with all of it that was like, okay, like even as weird as it feels, he didn't have a chance to take it the complete other route and be like, man, this is this is some bullshit, like I'm not here to I'm a guy, like I can be a guy. And he was like, no, like I'm going to do it, I'm going to do it to the best I can, and he was phenomenal. So that was that was huge.

quotes.speaker: Landry Shamet
quotes.summary_phrase: Landry Shamet on the team's growth and the Atlanta series
quotes.excerpt: They were still a young group obviously and it was kind of their first time getting in that position.
quotes.quote: I think with Atlanta, I think what it was, they were still a young group obviously and it was kind of their first time getting in that position and pushing the top dog to its limit really. And I think because I've been on some of those teams as well where you kind of like ride that high and you get like so invested in it and you reach a point where maybe like you tapped it out a little too early. And you know, and they were, they gave us probably some of the toughest challenges of the whole playoffs, so they were tremendous. But there's a point in that like, you talk about going into a game like that and you want to steal hope.

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on the Knicks' playoff performance and potential
quotes.excerpt: I felt like last year, you know, losing to Indiana that we could have beaten Indiana.
quotes.quote: I thought the year was not, you know, it wasn't a trajectory up. It was, it seemed to go up and down and up and down. So I was thinking, let's see if we get off to, you know, a good start. And I know that sometimes teams can take a jump, but it sometimes it takes something like that for it to occur, just as an observer, as a fan. So I felt like last year, you know, losing to Indiana that we could have beaten Indiana. We could have. And so, but I, I, I, I wasn't sure to see, you know, everything, I, I, I would see pockets of it, but not consistency, not like the way that you guys played in the playoffs, honestly.

quotes.speaker: Landry Shamet
quotes.summary_phrase: Landry Shamet on the impact of New York's fan culture
quotes.excerpt: When I see John on the street I got my, you know, like, so then you leave New York.
quotes.quote: There's a lot of like transplants who come and they live in New York, right? And they want to get the, oh, that's cool, like I need to, you know, when I see John on the street I got my, you know, like, so then you leave New York, even if you only lived here for two years, I'm a diehard Knicks fan now, you know, like it just the brand and being involved is like, it carries something. I don't know, it's crazy everywhere.

quotes.speaker: Landry Shamet
quotes.summary_phrase: Landry Shamet on the importance of bench depth
quotes.excerpt: If you're talking about a bench unit, especially in the NBA, call it what it is.
quotes.quote: If you're talking about a bench unit, especially in the NBA, call it what it is, like we're all fighting for our lives. Fighting for a job, fighting for the next one, fighting for whatever. So sometimes some ego and ulterior motives can creep in and you're kind of hoping like the guy in front of you, man, maybe, you know, maybe I'll get my chance like if he comes in and doesn't make his first couple looks like it's going to be me, right? So we had a group, me, Deuce, and Jordan at the beginning of the year could have been viewed as like this like logjam at the backup guard spot. And I felt like the type of guys we were, we were talking about it like there was never one point this season where any of us were like, man, I hope JC doesn't have it tonight so I can like, you know, like we had good guys. So one, I think you have to be lucky and two, that was definitely like a confidence boost for us because it's hard to prepare for.

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on the Knicks' comeback against the Bucks
quotes.excerpt: It reminded me of a game that I, well, I was before, yeah, before you guys were born.
quotes.quote: It reminded me of a game that I, well, I was before, yeah, before you guys were born, which was considered like one of the greatest games. After the Knicks won their first championship, they were playing the Milwaukee Bucks. It was Kareem's second season and they were up at the Garden, but there was no three-pointer by 18 and it was five minutes and like 30 something seconds left. And those games were blacked out in New York, so you could listen on radio. The Knicks were down by 18 and they scored 19 straight points and they held them scoreless. And that was almost impossible. It was almost impossible because Kareem had, you know, the skyhook and it's like there was no way he wasn't going to score one basket or two baskets. And they scored 19 straight points and they won, you know, and it was, and it reminded me of that game. I was like, this reminds me of that game that I only listened on radio to it. And I said, it can be done. This can be done, you know. I mean, you could get a three-pointer if you got fouled, right? But it was a different, it was harder when the lead was that big, but it did.

quotes.speaker: Landry Shamet
quotes.summary_phrase: Landry Shamet on the intelligence of Knicks fans
quotes.excerpt: Knicks fans in the Garden are some of the smartest fans.
quotes.quote: Knicks fans in the Garden are some of the smartest fans. So to your point, that five-point swing, I remember taking the charge and like, that was it. That was it. That's what I felt. I'm not saying it because Landry's here. My girlfriend, she said the same thing, like a few other people that they said when Jalen made that shot and then the charge, like she was, that's when it like, when it just takes, I think at MSG it just takes this like little like, all right.

quotes.speaker: Landry Shamet
quotes.summary_phrase: Landry Shamet on Stephen Curry's offensive awareness
quotes.excerpt: He's just searching throughout the game to find it and he does it, you know, multiple times.
quotes.quote: Jalen used to talk about that a lot, and we did an ep with Stephen Curry once where he was talking about this exact thing where it's like he's just searching throughout the game to find it and he does it, you know, multiple times a game usually, but he can sort of know when he's in it. Do you feel like that that has evolved for you over time?

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on his approach to work and life
quotes.excerpt: Validation is, I guess it's nice or whatever, but that's not the, the goal.
quotes.quote: Validation is, I guess it's nice or whatever, but that's not the, the goal. The goal is, you know, it's really the journey and what you're doing when you're doing it. It's the, it's in the doing that's the, the, the beautiful thing. It's not, you know, and then if the result is good and you like it, it's good. It's, it's, but in a way, we, we go from team to team because we, we don't have a regular job, you know, so you have to kind of just try to keep reinventing yourself as it goes on, as life goes on, and, uh, but you're, you don't have a stability in this thing.

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on the physicality of the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: I thought, wow, these guys are bigger than you guys, you know, and they're like so physical.
quotes.quote: When I first saw you guys play against San Antonio in that first game, I thought, wow, these guys are bigger than you guys, you know, and they're like so physical and they seem to be beating, especially the backcourt players up, you know, I was like, they're not calling any fouls. And I was like, wow. And then as it went on, I, I, I used to, because my, my dad was an amateur boxer, I, I'm a big, uh, boxing fan. I was thinking, oh, this is going to be like, this is like a prize fight. Like, you guys are like the shorter team in some ways, and we'll see if they, you know, they get underneath them.

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on the Knicks' team-first mentality
quotes.excerpt: It's a different, it's a different kind of win when you're like on a dynasty team.
quotes.quote: It's a different, it's a different kind of win when you're like on a dynasty team, like with Shaq and Kobe or something like that. It's a different kind of win. It's a collective win. And everybody in our group, I think, has dealt with their fair share in level of like being written off. Everyone. Talked about it.

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on his decision to pursue acting
quotes.excerpt: I'm done. I don't, I'm not doing this anymore.
quotes.quote: When I was 50 years old, I went to my PCP guy, Dr. Kutnick, and I said, you know, I'm done. I don't, I'm not doing this anymore. Because well, you know, he's a really funny guy. Well, why do you, why do you want to do? You know, I don't know, you know, he's, I said, I want to be a doctor. He said, well, you, you're 50 years old. I said, he said, I said, yeah, he said, you know how long it takes to become a doctor? And I said, yeah, like eight years. You good in science? I said, not really, you know, I said, but I have the right disposition, you know, to be a doctor. And then he talked, he said, well, you know, you do a good thing too. You help people when they're sick, they watch something you do, you make them laugh or you, you know, you give them the example of that finally that I, I needed. Like you guys gave them that and I think that's just, it's a beautiful thing.

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on the collaborative, team-oriented nature of his film projects
quotes.excerpt: It's a very team-oriented, collaborative process. That's the difference.

text_blocks.speaker: John Turturro
text_blocks.text: Everything I did with Spike, the people I worked with—Ernest Dickerson, Win Thomas, Ruth Carter—all those people, a lot of the actors, they've become my friends and I've worked with them again on other projects. It's a very team-oriented, collaborative process. That's the difference. If someone says, 'What do you think, Landry? What do you want to do? What is the best position for you to set up your shot?' you're included in it. You're not just a piece of furniture.

text_blocks.speaker: Cam Johnson
text_blocks.text: Do you see similarities between, say, Spike or the Coen brothers, whoever your favorite sort of collaborators you've worked with are? You're the team-oriented, collaborative sort.

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on the challenges of managing ego and space on a film set
quotes.excerpt: Sometimes a person wants to take up all the space, or whatever, and they're pushing you out.

text_blocks.speaker: Cam Johnson
text_blocks.text: Have you been on a project where there's been somebody on the project who's on a Jalen Game 5 run? You can just tell that they're levitating above anybody else that you've worked with?

text_blocks.speaker: John Turturro
text_blocks.text: Yeah, but that's usually spread across the film. One person comes in, they do something great, and then somehow the next person picks up on it. I think when you work with certain really great filmmakers, that can happen. You can form this kind of team spirit. It depends how much time you have to do that. I mean, when we did 'Do the Right Thing,' for example, we had a long rehearsal process and it was kind of awkward, but lots of great discussions, which was so unusual. You never have that in a film.

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on handling difficult actors and director-led conflict on set
quotes.excerpt: Sometimes a person wants to take up all the space, or whatever, and they're pushing you out.

text_blocks.speaker: Cam Johnson
text_blocks.text: Is that a very common challenge where you go on set and maybe it's your first time shooting with somebody and they're not really—

text_blocks.speaker: John Turturro
text_blocks.text: Yeah, well, sometimes a person wants to take up all the space, or whatever, and they're pushing you out of the frame. You're like, 'Well, this person is very needy.' Then I just go talk to Spike or somebody and say, 'Listen, man, I know you want me in the frame, but he's pushing me out of the frame. So what am I going to do? Like, push him? I have to dance around the guy or whatever.' But that's ego and stuff like that. Usually, I go to the director and I'll say, 'Listen, you want me to do that? I'll do it.' Sometimes you do something that the director asks you, and it bothers the other actor, but a director's asks are coming from up top to do it.

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on Denzel Washington's performance in 'He Got Game'
quotes.excerpt: Denzel felt really proud that he scored a basket against him and that really pissed Ray off.

text_blocks.speaker: John Turturro
text_blocks.text: I only did a couple of days on that. I had to shoot with Ray Allen for a couple of days. He was—you know, you can shoot. I said, 'Yeah, I played high school basketball.' But yeah, that was fun. He did a great job. Actually, Spike talked to me before. He wanted Iverson brought in, but Iverson didn't even show up for his audition or something like that. He didn't even show up. I said, 'I think you're going to have a hard time lasting with those guys.' I said, 'You better get someone who's going to be...' But Ray did a really—he worked with a coach, and he did a really good job. He was really lovely to work with. I know that Denzel felt really proud that he scored a basket against him and that really pissed Ray off.

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on Denzel Washington's method acting during 'He Got Game'
quotes.excerpt: The whole time they were shooting the movie, he would pretend like he was terrible.

text_blocks.speaker: Cam Johnson
text_blocks.text: Did you ever hear that story?

text_blocks.speaker: John Turturro
text_blocks.text: Yeah, they were filming, right? And Denzel—they were like, 'All right, we're just going to kind of go through the motions.' Denzel was a good basketball player. He played Mount Vernon, like a really good—I might have even played in college—good basketball player. And the whole time they were shooting the movie, the entire time because they were shooting it chronologically, so they were shooting that scene at the end, the whole time, anytime they were shooting around, he would pretend like he was terrible. So he would just be like missing on purpose and he would be bricking—he would just be bricking every shot, making sure Ray didn't see it. So when they do the final scene, he scores the first three points and Ray just gets fucking pissed. And he understands, he like realizes what's happening and then he just snaps. And so you could see the anger. You could see him, he's just like, he's like, 'Fuck that,' like—

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Johnson on the importance of routine and minimizing decision-making during game days
quotes.excerpt: I think for me the reason why I do it is that it reduces thinking.

text_blocks.speaker: Cam Johnson
text_blocks.text: I try to plan it out. I think for me the reason why I do it is that it reduces thinking, so I don't have to make any decisions from the moment I wake up on a game day until, you know, the only decisions I have to make are in a game, really. So I think it helps me just kind of minimize like any excess like energy I'm pouring out.

text_blocks.speaker: John Turturro
text_blocks.text: That's probably the version of your work that's the most—because like in a week, if you're doing a residency somewhere or whatever, like you guys are doing a play somewhere, how many shows a week are you doing?

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Johnson on the unique challenges of playing NBA Finals games on the road
quotes.excerpt: I think there was some advantage to being the road team in this Finals, for sure.

text_blocks.speaker: Cam Johnson
text_blocks.text: I think there was some advantage to being the road team in this Finals, for sure, because it was such a circus. I'd never seen that level of media coverage. People don't really think about that part. If you're going to have—like we didn't practice at our practice facility at home when we were here. It all had to be at the Garden because it was open for media. So even that, just like—but when you're on the road, to your point, it's just a road game. Like, it's just kind of—

text_blocks.speaker: John Turturro
text_blocks.text: And they're staying up in the boonies, so it's like you're so far up. You're in San Antonio, you're so far away from everything. It's like hill country, so you can kind of block out. It's a little more chill than being in this where anytime you walk outside, everything is—

quotes.speaker: John Turturro
quotes.summary_phrase: John Turturro on the community experience of walking across the Brooklyn Bridge
quotes.excerpt: It's a great thing when it's—you feel like you're part of a community.

text_blocks.speaker: John Turturro
text_blocks.text: So we walked together over the Brooklyn Bridge to go to the parade. And it was great, all these people walking over the over the Brooklyn Bridge in Knicks jerseys, you know, going to the parade. And I was thinking like, 'Well, this is what it's about.' Like, the whole city, like we're all walking, you know, to to to cheer you guys on. And it's a great thing when it's—you feel like you're part of a community, which you don't always feel like in New York City.

text_blocks.speaker: Cam Johnson
text_blocks.text: Well said. I think that's a great way to close it.
